lesson: Scaling up beat single neurons. Late-layer (L21-27) MLP columns ranked by |cos| to a category's mean unembedding direction, minus 0.5x the best other category, made big clean clusters on qwenmath7b: ordinal L24 64/256/512 dropped the target .91/.91/.92, number-word L25 256 .49, month L25 256 .43, colour L24 256 .38. Random same-size parts mostly stayed under .1, though screen draws occasionally reached .18-.36.

Rank by subspace, then penalise. Scoring units by norm fraction in a category's unembedding subspace finds shared hubs. The L23 weekday-subspace top 64 hit weekday .85 but also month .58 and number-word .39, so it could not pass. Subtracting the max fraction in the other categories' subspaces separated a clean weekday part: L23 64 at .63 and 128 at .70.

Mid layers (L8-18) need seed growth, not unembedding projection. Take 1-3 attribution seed units and add the units whose gate, up and down weights are most cosine-similar (summed). That gave clean 64-128 unit clusters, e.g. ordinal L9 .73, L10 .76, L13 .46 and number-word L9 .64, while per-layer unembedding cosines there were noise-level (top-64 cos about .04).

Head groups worked when OV circuits showed copy or successor structure and attribution agreed. Examples: L24 Greek copy heads [20,21,23,27] at .54, and ordinal successor-OV heads at L14/16/19/21 at .63/.82/.97/.58. Redundancy matters: ablating whole KV group 2 or 3 in L24 did nothing for Greek, but removing heads across both groups dropped it .54.

Weight-only signals that failed causally: (1) L21/L22 heads whose OV maps digits onto the even-vs-odd direction (|corr| up to .91) had zero effect on parity. (2) The parity-attributed L27 units 12772 and 6696 are a/an and vowel-onset writers, and ablating such clusters at L26 improved parity by .21. (3) Code, CJK, Spanish and German writer clusters left the code and multilingual built-ins unchanged (<.05). (4) L0 heads and whole blocks wrecked everything.

Near-miss leaks were common, often by tiny margins. Swapping out the one head or unit carrying the leaking skill (seen in attribution) usually fixed it. For example, L22 parity heads [1,2,3,24] failed with number-word at .1082 against a .108 limit. Also, with few control items the controls move in coarse steps (Greek .0303), so aim for a target drop above .25 to keep margin.
